Method of Attack: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attack dropping a legitimate signed vulnerable kernel driver (zamguard64.sys or zam64.sys) to gain kernel-level privileges and terminate antivirus, XDR, and EDR software processes
Requires administrative privileges and user acceptance of UAC prompt
Uses vulnerable Zemana anti-malware driver to kill user-mode security processes
Attack Vector: Administrative privileges on targeted Windows systems
User Account Control (UAC) prompt tricking user to accept
Dropping and loading vulnerable signed kernel driver
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of vulnerable Zemana anti-malware kernel driver files zamguard64.sys or zam64.sys with random 4-10 character names in C:\Windows\System32\
Detection by a single anti-malware scanning engine on VirusTotal
YARA and Sigma rules shared by Florian Roth and Nasreddine Bencherchali for detection
